To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
MHC class I molecules are inducible in neurons of the CNS and are recognized by virus‐specific CTL, which kill neurons in an Fas/Fas‐ligand‐dependent manner.
neuronal MHC class molecules expressed in electrically silenced neurons are recognized and killed by virus‐specific CTL via Fas‐mediated apoptosis.
MHC class I molecules expressed on electrically silenced hippocampal neurons are functional in mediating Fas‐dependent, but perforin‐independent, killing by CTL.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the immunological function and the mechanism of killing of neuronal MHC‐class I‐expressing target cells by virus‐specific CTL.
the immunological function(s) of MHC class‐I antigens expressed in neurons of the brain, which are known to induce apoptosis of activated T lymphocytes.

a novel pathway for neuronal killing by CD8+ CTL which is dependent upon the expression of MHC class I molecules, the Fas ligand (FasL), but is independent of perforin‐mediated cytotoxic granule exocytosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the neuronal Fas/Fas‐L pathway is a novel mechanism of CTL‐mediated killing of neurons.
the neuronal FasL/Fas pathway is involved in the MHC class I restricted killing of neurons by CD8+ CTL, while the perforin pathway is not.
MHC class I expression in neurons of the CNS renders these cells susceptible to Fas‐mediated apoptosis by CD8+ T cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

MHC class I molecules on hippocampal neurons can function as targets for cytotoxic T lymphocyte‐mediated killing, but that the mechanism of killing is different from that observed with other cell types.
MHC class I molecules expressed in the brain by neurons are not only involved in the induction of immune tolerance, but also in the elimination of virus infected or otherwise damaged cells.
neurons, which have been rendered susceptible to attack by CTL by induction of MHC class 1 and Fas molecules, are killed by Fas‐mediated apoptosis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
neuronal MHC class‐I expression is not sufficient for the induction of cytotoxic T cell‐mediated neuronal death.

neuronal MHC class 1 antigens, induced under conditions of electrically suppressed synaptic activity, render hippocampal neurons susceptible to attack by virus‐specific CTL, which kill the cells by triggering apoptosis through the FasL/Fas, but not the granule/perforin pathway.
the neuronal MHC class‐I molecules are not involved in the presentation of antigens to CD4+ T cells.
